overview: The Icon component renders a Lucide icon as an inline SVG, identified by name. The component adapts its default color between light and dark themes using design tokens, and is intended for use wherever a scalable, accessible icon glyph is needed. For interactive icon-only actions, prefer the Icon Button component instead. For React components, use the `lucide-react` library instead.

whenToUse: To add inline iconography that supports or replaces a text label
When a Lucide icon name maps directly to the intended meaning
For decorative glyphs that reinforce UI state (success, warning, navigation)
do: Use semantic size tokens (inline, control, standalone, large) instead of arbitrary pixel values — tokens keep sizing consistent across the system
Set aria-hidden="true" on purely decorative icons so screen readers skip them
Add an accessible label to the surrounding interactive element when the icon is the only content
Pair icons with visible text labels wherever space allows — icon-only patterns require extra accessibility care
dont: Don't use pkts-icon for interactive icon-only actions — use the Icon Button component instead, which handles focus and accessible labeling
Don't rely on icon color alone to convey meaning — always pair with a text label or accessible description
Don't pass arbitrary pixel sizes when a semantic token covers the use case
